text: The Patriots are navigating a bittersweet week of transitions and roster questions heading into their Week 2 home opener against the Steelers: Stephon Gilmore, the franchise's 2019 Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro, signed a one-day contract Friday to retire as a New England Patriot, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest cornerbacks in franchise history, while on the injury front, running back TreVeyon Henderson is expected to suit up Sunday after missing the opener with an ankle injury and said he's "ready to go," though the Patriots could be without starting cornerback Carlton Davis III, who is officially listed as questionable. In lighter news, Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri will attempt a Guinness World Record kick at Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps as part of the team's promotional push for their upcoming game in Munich, and off the field, owner Robert Kraft confirmed he had Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's shows at Gillette Stadium, citing the artist's "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery" as deeply offensive to the Jewish community. The Patriots host Pittsburgh on Sunday at 1 PM ET as they look to bounce back from their Week 1 loss.
